components.css: .ds-tip { padding: 12px 16px 4px; background: var(--paper); color: var(--ink); border: 1px solid var(--ink); outline: 1px solid var(--hair); outline-offset: 3px; font-family: var(--sans); font-size: var(--step-0); line-height: 1.65; } .ds-tip p { margin: 0 0 0.7em; } .ds-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-mark { display: inline-grid; color: var(--gold-ink); } .ds-label { font-size: var(--step--1); font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-head a { margin-left: auto; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink-2); } .ds-head a:hover { color: var(--gold-ink); }

components.css: .ds-sym { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px 18px; font: 400 14px/1.4 var(--sans); color: var(--ink); } .ds-sym li { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-route { width: 24px; height: 4px; background: var(--gold); } .ds-sq, .ds-ci { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 22px; height: 22px; font: 700 11px/1 var(--sans); } .ds-sq { background: var(--ink); color: #fff; } .ds-ci { border: 2px solid var(--ink); border-radius: 50%; color: var(--ink); }

components.css: .ds-idx { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(170px, 1fr)); border-block: 1px solid var(--ink); font-family: var(--sans); } .ds-idx li + li { border-left: 1px solid var(--hair); } .ds-idx a { display: grid; gap: 2px; padding: 12px 24px; color: var(--ink); text-decoration: none; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.25; } .ds-idx a:hover { background: var(--field); } .ds-idx a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--gold); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-n { color: var(--ink-3); font-weight: 400; font-size: 13px; }

narrative.overview:
Each trip is a printed topographic survey sheet in the manner of IGN or Swisstopo. The map and its legend are the document; the page is framed, ruled and numbered like a map sheet, with a running head carrying sheet number and coordinates, a title cartouche, a legend box with the export actions, and region sheets that each open on a heavy rule. The reading column inside that frame stays plain: one reading face, real contrast, a 62ch measure.

The world is navy ink on white drafting paper. Ink draws every line, type and border. Gold is the route's colour and the warning's colour; it never decorates. Depth comes from rules, not surfaces: double borders, single 1px ink rules between cells, hairlines inside them. Corners are square because printed sheets are square; the only circles are the map's own sight symbols.

Density is that of a map margin: small tracked capitals for legend and field labels, tabular monospace for every coordinate and EXIF value, and generous whitespace only in the reading column. Photography is shown at native 3:2 or 2:3, never cropped, captioned as numbered plates.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled double border frames the whole page (2px ink, 6px gap, 1px ink).
Navy ink for all line and type; gold reserved for route, warnings, tip marks, focus and the "located" flash.
Square corners everywhere; circles only as the sight map symbol.
Overpass for everything, Overpass Mono for coordinates and camera data.
Grid cells separated by 1px ink rules and 0.18-alpha ink hairlines, never by cards or shadows.
Map tiles (OpenTopoMap) desaturated and shifted toward navy by a CSS filter so the gold route is the only warm line.

rules.name: The Two-Ink Rule
rules.body: Navy draws; gold marks the way. If a gold element is not a route, a warning, a tip mark, a focus or a located state, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Gold-Ink Split Rule
rules.body: Raw gold (#b08d3e) never carries text. Any gold glyph or word at text size uses gold-ink.

rules.name: The Tinted Tiles Rule
rules.body: Third-party map tiles are always filtered to the sheet (`grayscale(1) sepia(0.35) hue-rotate(180deg) saturate(1.4) contrast(0.7) brightness(1.18)`), so no tile colour competes with the gold route.

rules.name: The Copyable-Number Rule
rules.body: Any value a reader might copy or compare (coordinates, EXIF, map ticks) is set in Overpass Mono with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Label-Carries-Data Rule
rules.body: Tracked capitals name a field or carry data (sheet number, "Région 2 / 6 · Jours 3–5", "Planche 04"). A label that names nothing does not get set.

rules.name: The Ruled-Not-Raised Rule
rules.body: Page surfaces never cast shadows; separate them with a rule of the right weight. Shadow is allowed only for map overlays.

dos: Do frame every trip page in the ruled double border (2px ink, 6px gap, 1px ink).
Do separate cells with 1px ink rules and hairlines (rgb(18 41 79 / 0.18)) rather than background tints.
Do set coordinates, EXIF and map ticks in Overpass Mono with tabular figures.
Do use gold-ink (#7d6224) for any gold text or small glyph; keep raw gold (#b08d3e) for lines, fills and the focus ring.
Do filter any map tiles to the navy sheet so the gold route is the only warm line.
Do show photos at native 3:2 or 2:3 with their plate number and EXIF line.
donts: Don't round corners on boxes, buttons, tips or map controls; the circle belongs to the sight symbol only.
Don't put drop shadows on page surfaces; shadow is for map pins and popups.
Don't use gold for decoration, headings, backgrounds or body links.
Don't crop photos or force them into a uniform ratio.
Don't set a tracked-capital label above or below a heading unless it carries a field name or data.
